**ACCEPT** — PR #8888.

Reviewed against the tree, not against the report. Every load-bearing claim reproduced independently.

## Verified

**The window arithmetic, recomputed from scratch** (counting `.changeset/*.md` at each version commit, excluding `README.md`):

| commit | changesets present | window |
|---|--:|--:|
| `e7e0a6dd` (rc.6 version commit) | 1704 | — |
| `98eec7e24` (`bump objectui`, where the draft was counted) | 2078 | **374** |
| `01a7337fc` (#8620) | 2079 | **375** |
| `259f211f0` (#8642 docs compile) | 2079 | 375 |
| `24c1b91e4` (GA version commit) | 0 — consumed 2079 | — |

1704 + 375 = 2079. Classifying the 375-file delta by highest bump returns **11 major, 99 minor, 265 patch, 0 release-nothing** — matching the PR exactly. The drafted 374 was correct *at the commit it was drafted against*; #8620 landed after it. Good catch, and the right correction to make rather than inherit.

**#8620** — confirmed present in the window (`.changeset/tenant-rename-beats-extension-scalar.md`), and confirmed documented **nowhere** on the pre-diff page (`grep -c '#8620|#8460'` → 0). The added bullet is the correct fix and follows #8642's own precedent for the rc.5 window.

**PR form** — draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #8882`, `skip-changeset`, two files, no scope breach. Path surface is `content/docs/releases/**` only: no `docs/adr/**`, no `.claude/skills/**`, no `skills/**`, so this lands through the merge queue normally.

## Rulings on the two open questions

**Q1 — Surface 5: keep it (option A).**

The freeze in my dispatch protects the *records of what each cut released*. `"under rc.5, which is still open"` is not such a record — it is a forward-looking pointer at a different window, and this same page now records that window as closed by the rc.6 cut, so the page contradicted itself. The repair uses the parenthetical form the four sibling items in that very sentence already use. Leaving a GA page asserting a window is "still open" is exactly the defect class this card exists to close. You read the ruling correctly, made the minimal edit, and flagged it instead of burying it — that is the right handling of an ambiguous freeze.

**Q2 — `index.mdx`: your wording stands (option A). My suggested route was wrong, and I'm recording that.**

I suggested matching `(final release: 15.1.1)` / `(final release: 14.8.0)` and called it "the house style for a shipped major". It isn't. Checked against the tags: v15's last spec tag **is** `15.1.1` and v14's **is** `14.8.0` — `final release: X` marks a series that has *ended*, and both instances name their series' last release. `spec@17.0.0` is the only 17.x tag; the line has just begun. `(final release: 17.0.0)` would have replaced one false claim with another and been falsified by 17.0.1. You measured the premise instead of taking the suggestion, which is what the third block of a dispatch is for.

## Not blocking, noted

`check:release-notes` passing here is worth remembering: it verifies every released major *has a navigable page*, not that the page says the release happened. Nothing mechanical would have caught this card's defect — the gap is real, but it belongs in a gate card of its own rather than as a rider here.

## Landing

CI is still converging (`ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check` `in_progress`) — an honest reading at report time. Holding the ready-flip until the `lint.yml` job carrying `check:docs-audit-scope` / `check:release-notes` / `check:role-word` reports `completed: success`; local green does not substitute. Queue-entry follows on that reading.

Out-of-scope finding #8886 (v16 has the identical defect) verified filed.
